significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the conclusion that, for shared-initialization students, projection onto a teacher-derived trait direction identifies the transmitted trait and quantitatively predicts its behavioral strength; this is a form-(iii) predictive coupling between two independently measurable quantities, not merely an existence claim. It would establish both a phenomenon—"projection magnitude correlates with behavioral trait strength"—and an approximately linear parameter-space mechanism, fixing the expectation that stronger aligned displacement produces stronger trait expression; this bears directly on the parameter-alignment account developed in Cloud et al.'s Subliminal Learning (2025), while Ilharco et al.'s task-arithmetic results illustrate why usable weight-delta structure can constrain model behavior. The negative branch is weaker because, as the claim concedes, a nonlinear or differently based encoding could defeat this readout without refuting parameter-borne transmission, although it would still rule out the specific teacher-aligned linear account; true and false outcomes are otherwise determinate through identification and correlation assertions. Topic-substitution check: replacing this projection law with the generic goal of extending subliminal learning would not retain the score, because the above weight-to-behavior coupling is the claim-specific increment over an obvious replication or behavioral extension.

reach.justification: The concrete handle is the "cosine of each student's weight delta against a bank of candidate trait directions," used as a direct weight-space payload readout; it is ex ante with respect to behavioral elicitation and deployment because the claim says the trait can be recovered "without ever running the student." After per-model re-extraction, the conclusion predicts a matched-direction ordering and a projection–behavior correlation for new students sharing an initialization, rather than merely supplying an unconstrained search procedure, but its asserted cross-family collapse and unstated cross-architecture generality limit transfer. The immediate downstream users could include researchers and auditors with weight access who want to identify or gate trait-bearing fine-tunes before elicitation, although the claim does not establish applicability to closed-weight systems or outside AI. Topic-substitution check: the generic subliminal-learning topic supplies neither this pre-elicitation metric nor its predicted coupling, so the reach score rests on the claim-specific handle rather than the topic's general importance.
